answer: Anti-Sybil here meters grader minutes, not key count. Each new identity locks a stake sized to the rolling median cost of one graded answer; that stake is the anchor. Answers leave a quill record of mechanism claims scored 0–3; a jury median below 2 forfeits an ember fraction of the stake into a burn pool. Empty templates fail fast, so mass cloning pays stake×N plus burn×fails — the thousandth sock is strictly more expensive than the first.
